messages.author: ec7010d530c9f38f
messages.subject: Inbreds and inferring gender
parts:
Dear all,

I am having problems with the callXXorXY method that is used in doing naive genotyping as a preparation for TumorBoost. At a certain stage in the naive genotyping (see this vignette) you have to infer the gender of your samples with the callXXorXY-method. The problem is that based on BAFs from chrX it thinks the sample is XY, but based on BAFs from chrY it thinks the sample is not XY. I have a theory why this is happening:

As far as I understand it correctly, this method uses findPeaksAndValleys() to find out how much peaks there are in a density-plot of BAFs at chrX and chrY. If there are two peaks in chrX, it assumes the sample is XY. Then it does the same for BAFs at chrY and if the two answers are the same, the program continues and otherwise it fails.

This method works perfectly for "normal" samples but when it comes to inbreds (so samples that (theoretically) are homozygous at every locus in the genome) I think it is causing problems. Assume you have a female inbred sample (so XX). Normally, XX-genotypes give rise to three peaks in the BAF-density plots: at 0 (for AA), 0.5 (for AB) and at 1 (for BB). But in the case of inbreds (where the only possibilities are AA or BB because both chromosomes are identical copies) there will be only two peaks: at 0 and at 1. Though this sample is truly female, the callXXorXY will think it is male because it translates 2 peaks to the sample being XY. At the same time, at calls the same female inbred sample XX when it relies on BAFS at chrY because there will not be 2 peaks in the BAF-density plot (as there is no Y-chromosome in this sample...). This causes the callXXorXY program to terminate throwing the following exception:

Error in list(`callXXorXY(betaN[is23], betaN[is24], adjust = adjust, from = 0, to = 1)` = <environment>,  : 
  
[2012-03-15 11:37:02] Exception: Allele B fractions for ChrX and ChrY are inconsistent.
...

What is the best solution to this issue? Setting the gender manually? Or make the callXXorXY only use BAF's from chrY to infer the gender (as female inbreds do not have Y (so not 2 peaks) but male inbreds to have one copy (so 2 peaks) of Y)? Or anything else????

I might be mistaking about some things and I would be happy to hear any discussion points about this theory :-)

Irsan

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Inbreds and inferring gender
parts:
Hi,

sorry for the delay on this one. It is seems that you have a special
case that we didn't consider when we designed the naive genotyping
algorithm. I can have a look at this, but in order to do that I'd
need some example data. Would you mind making the data for one
tumor-normal pair available for download? This means the two
*,fracB.asb and the two *,total.asb files in
totalAndFracBData/Retino,ACC,ra,-XY,BPN,-XY,AVG,FLN,-XY/MOUSEDIVm520650/
for this pair. You can email me the download link offline (not the
mailing list).

/Henrik
